title: Khon Kaen International Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Weekend Was Like
seo_title: Khon Kaen International Marathon 2027 Review | Thailand
meta_description: Khon Kaen International Marathon review: a runner's account of the January 2026 race weekend, a 12C start, water every 2-3 km and a 3am marathon start.
dek: Khon Kaen's January race weekend runs from a 5 km on Saturday to the marathon on Sunday. Here is what the 2026 edition was like, from a runner who did two races that weekend.
verdict: The Khon Kaen International Marathon is a well-organised university-city race weekend with a serious international field. In January 2026 a visiting runner found a super-organised race-kit pickup with helpful volunteers, water every 2-3 km, closed roads with police at intersections, and students cheering on the campus loop [1]. The weather helped: a cool air mass meant a 12°C start [1]. The marathon started at 3am and the half at 4am, with runners from 56 countries and Ethiopian and Kenyan runners at the front [1]. The main complaint was crowding at the start of the 10 km [1]. If you want a friendly, cool-weather race weekend in north-east Thailand, it is a strong choice.

sections.heading: The Race Weekend
paragraphs: The event runs over two days: shorter races on Saturday, including a 5 km on the Khon Kaen University campus, and the main races on Sunday, the marathon, half marathon and a 'mini marathon' of about 11.5 km [1]. Sunday's field included runners from 56 countries, with Ethiopian and Kenyan runners leading and a men's winning time of about 2:18 [1].

Race-kit pickup at the Golden Jubilee Convention Hall was, in the runner's words, super organised, with maps, English-speaking helpers and coloured tape on the floor leading to the right table, and an expo of 50 to 60 running vendors [1].

sections.heading: What It Was Like to Run
paragraphs: Saturday's 5 km started at 6am on closed, tree-lined roads through the university's agricultural areas, finishing at a point-to-point finish with 50 to 60 food stalls [1]. The distance on the bib said 5.4 km but the timed course was changed at the last minute to 4.8 km [1].

On Sunday the marathon started at 3am and the half marathon at 4am, with a 3 hour 30 minute cut-off, after corrals, fireworks and an organised bag drop, though with long toilet queues [1]. The 10 km runner spent the first 2 to 3 km dodging runners who had started too far forward and people already walking, then ran through the city and a loop around the campus, with police at intersections, water every 2 to 3 km, sports drinks and fruit, and cheering students [1].

sections.heading: Weather
paragraphs: A cool air mass over Thailand that weekend meant a 12°C start, 16°C before sunrise and the mid-20s by mid-morning [1]. January is the cool, dry season in the north-east, and the early starts are designed to use it [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes. By this runner's account, the organisation is strong, the volunteers are helpful, the aid stations are frequent and the weather in January can be genuinely cool.

Position yourself carefully in your corral if you want to run a time, since the start of the shorter races can be congested, and plan transport to the start: there was no shuttle for the Saturday race.
This review is compiled from a runner's own account of the 2026 race weekend. It is not a race report by this site, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: What is the Khon Kaen International Marathon like?
faqs.answer: A well-organised race weekend, by one 2026 runner's account: super-organised kit pickup, water every 2-3 km, sports drinks and fruit, closed roads with police at intersections, and students cheering on the university campus loop.

faqs.question: What time does the Khon Kaen Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2026 the marathon started at 3am, the half marathon at 4am with a 3 hour 30 minute cut-off, and the 10 km at 4.45am. The shorter Saturday races start at 6am.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the Khon Kaen Marathon?
faqs.answer: It can be cool. In January 2026 a cool air mass meant a 12°C start, 16°C before sunrise and the mid-20s by mid-morning, much cooler than most Southeast Asian races.
